newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia bank gets permit to sell ADRs to foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Russia bank gets permit to sell ADRs to foreigners.

text.p: One of Russia's biggest banks, MAKB Vozrozhdeniye, has received permission from the central bank to sell its American Depositary Receipts to foreign investors, Vozrozhdeniye said on Monday.

Vozrozhdeniye received U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission permission to issue Level One ADRs in July, but by Russian law a bank cannot sell its shares to foreigners without central bank permission.
Vozrozhdeniye's ADRs will cover not more than three percent of 25.54 billion rouble authorised capital, it said in a statement.
One ADR equals one ordinary share.
Bank of New York will be Vozrozhdeniye's depositary.
Earlier this month the central bank permitted two other Russian banks, Inkombank and Menatep to sell ADRs to foreigners.
